The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

impl Widget for Paragraph<'_> {
    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
        Widget::render(&self, area, buf);
    }
}

impl Widget for &Paragraph<'_> {
    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
        let area = area.intersection(buf.area);
        buf.set_style(area, self.style);
        self.block.as_ref().render(area, buf);
        let inner = self.block.inner_if_some(area);
        self.render_paragraph(inner, buf);
    }
}

impl Paragraph<'_> {
    fn render_paragraph(&self, text_area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
        if text_area.is_empty() {
            return;
        }

        buf.set_style(text_area, self.style);
        let styled = self.text.iter().map(|line| {
            let graphemes = line.styled_graphemes(self.text.style);
            let alignment = line.alignment.unwrap_or(self.alignment);
            (graphemes, alignment)
        });

        if let Some(Wrap { trim }) = self.wrap {
            let mut line_composer = WordWrapper::new(styled, text_area.width, trim);
            // compute the lines iteratively until we reach the desired scroll offset.
            for _ in 0..self.scroll.y {
                if line_composer.next_line().is_none() {
                    return;
                }
            }
            render_lines(line_composer, text_area, buf);
        } else {
            // avoid unnecessary work by skipping directly to the relevant line before rendering
            let lines = styled.skip(self.scroll.y as usize);
            let mut line_composer = LineTruncator::new(lines, text_area.width);
            line_composer.set_horizontal_offset(self.scroll.x);
            render_lines(line_composer, text_area, buf);
        }
    }
}

fn render_lines<'a, C: LineComposer<'a>>(mut composer: C, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
    let mut y = 0;
    while let Some(ref wrapped) = composer.next_line() {
        render_line(wrapped, area, buf, y);
        y += 1;
        if y >= area.height {
            break;
        }
    }
}

fn render_line(wrapped: &WrappedLine<'_, '_>, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, y: u16) {
    let mut x = get_line_offset(wrapped.width, area.width, wrapped.alignment);
    for StyledGrapheme { symbol, style } in wrapped.graphemes {
        let width = symbol.cell_width();
        if width == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        // Make sure to overwrite any previous character with a space (rather than a zero-width)
        let symbol = if symbol.is_empty() { " " } else { symbol };
        let position = Position::new(area.left() + x, area.top() + y);
        buf[position].set_symbol(symbol).set_style(*style);
        x += width;
    }
}

    /// - [`Viewport::Fullscreen`]: clears the entire terminal.
    /// - [`Viewport::Fixed`]: clears only the viewport region.
    /// - [`Viewport::Inline`]: clears after the viewport's origin, leaving any content above the
    ///   viewport untouched.
    ///
    /// Current behavior: for [`Viewport::Inline`], clearing runs from the viewport origin through
    /// the end of the visible display area, not just the viewport's rectangle. This is an
    /// implementation detail rather than a contract; do not rely on it.
    ///
    /// This preserves the backend's current cursor position.
    ///
    /// This also resets the "previous" buffer so the next [`Terminal::flush`] redraws the full
    /// viewport.
    ///
    /// [`Terminal::resize`]: crate::terminal::Terminal::resize
    ///
    /// Implementation note: this uses [`ClearType::AfterCursor`] starting at the viewport origin.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), B::Error> {
        let original_cursor = self.backend.get_cursor_position()?;
        self.clear_viewport()?;
        self.backend.set_cursor_position(original_cursor)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Clears according to the current viewport and resets the back buffer.
    ///
    /// Unlike [`Terminal::clear`], this does not snapshot and restore the backend cursor
    /// position. Callers that need to preserve the cursor should do so outside this helper.
    pub(super) fn clear_viewport(&mut self) -> Result<(), B::Error> {
        match self.viewport {
            Viewport::Fullscreen => self.backend.clear_region(ClearType::All)?,
            Viewport::Inline(_) => {
                self.backend
                    .set_cursor_position(self.viewport_area.as_position())?;
                self.backend.clear_region(ClearType::AfterCursor)?;
            }
            Viewport::Fixed(_) => {
                let area = self.viewport_area;
                self.clear_fixed_viewport(area)?;
            }
        }
        // Reset the back buffer to make sure the next update will redraw everything.
        self.buffers[1 - self.current].reset();
        Ok(())
    }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FramePos {
    pub id: StackId,
    pub x: u16,
    pub width: u16,
}

/// Layout of all frames, row by row (row index == depth).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct FrameLayout {
    pub rows: Vec<Vec<FramePos>>,
    /// Number of rows that fit in the flame graph area.
    pub page: usize,
    /// Number of rows that actually contain frames.
    pub row_count: usize,
}

impl FrameLayout {
    pub fn find(&self, id: StackId) -> Option<(usize, FramePos)> {
        for (row, frames) in self.rows.iter().enumerate() {

                return Some((row, *f));
            }
        }
        None
    }

    pub fn visible(&self, id: StackId) -> bool {

    }

//! Rendering of the application state.

use ratatui::layout::{Alignment, Constraint, Layout, Rect};
use ratatui::style::{Color, Modifier, Style};
use ratatui::text::{Line, Span, Text};
use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Borders, Cell, Padding, Paragraph, Row, Table, TableState, Wrap};
use ratatui::Frame;
use std::time::Instant;

use crate::app::{App, FramePos, SortColumn, View};
use crate::flame::StackId;

const LEFT_WIDTH: u16 = 20;
const RIGHT_TEXT: &str = concat!("flamelens v", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));

const SELECTED_BG: Color = Color::Rgb(250, 250, 250);
const MATCH_BG: (u8, u8, u8) = (10, 35, 150);
const MATCH_FG: Color = Color::Rgb(225, 10, 10);
const DARK_FG: Color = Color::Rgb(10, 10, 10);
const LIGHT_FG: Color = Color::Rgb(225, 225, 225);
const TABLE_HIGHLIGHT_BG: Color = Color::Rgb(65, 65, 65);

fn title_style() -> Style {
    Style::default()
        .fg(Color::Yellow)
        .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)
}

fn bold() -> Style {
    Style::default().add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)
}

/// A bottom section: a titled separator followed by some text.
struct Section<'a> {
    title: &'static str,
    text: Text<'a>,
}

impl Section<'_> {
    fn height(&self, width: u16) -> u16 {
        let lines = Paragraph::new(self.text.clone())
            .wrap(Wrap { trim: true })
            .line_count(width);
        1 + lines as u16
    }

    fn render(&self, area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame) {
        let block = Block::new()
            .borders(Borders::TOP)
            .title(Span::styled(self.title, title_style()));
        let paragraph = Paragraph::new(self.text.clone())
            .wrap(Wrap { trim: true })
            .block(block);
        frame.render_widget(paragraph, area);
    }
}

fn separator(area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame) {
    if area.height == 0 {
        return;
    }
    frame.render_widget(Block::new().borders(Borders::TOP), area);
}

pub fn render(app: &mut App, frame: &mut Frame) {
    let area = frame.area();
    if area.width == 0 || area.height == 0 {
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Header geometry
    let right_width = RIGHT_TEXT.len() as u16;
    let (left_w, mid_w, right_w) = {
        let right_w = right_width.min(area.width);
        let rest = area.width - right_w;
        let left_w = LEFT_WIDTH.min(rest);
        (left_w, rest - left_w, right_w)
    };
    let header_lines = Paragraph::new(app.title.as_str())
        .wrap(Wrap { trim: true })
        .line_count(mid_w.saturating_sub(4)) as u16;
    let top_needed = 2 + header_lines;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Bottom sections
    let sections = bottom_sections(app);
    let mut needs: Vec<u16> = sections.iter().map(|s| s.height(area.width)).collect();
    needs.push(2); // key hints
    let bottom_needed: u16 = needs.iter().sum();

    let chunks = Layout::vertical([
        Constraint::Length(top_needed),
        Constraint::Min(0),
        Constraint::Length(bottom_needed),
    ])
    .split(area);
    let (top_area, main_area, bottom_area) = (chunks[0], chunks[1], chunks[2]);
    let top_h = top_area.height;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Top: separator, header, separator
    let sep1_h = top_h.min(1);
    let sep2_h = (top_h - sep1_h).min(1);
    separator(Rect::new(area.x, top_area.y, area.width, sep1_h), frame);
    separator(
        Rect::new(
            area.x,
            top_area.y + top_h.saturating_sub(1),
            area.width,
            sep2_h,
        ),
        frame,
    );
    // The header is drawn starting on the second row; when space is tight it
    // overlaps the separator below it (which is drawn first).
    let header_area = Rect::new(area.x, top_area.y + 1, area.width, top_h);
    render_header(app, header_area, left_w, mid_w, right_w, frame);

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Main area
    match app.view {
        View::Flamegraph => render_flamegraph(app, main_area, frame),
        View::Top => render_table(app, main_area, frame),
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Bottom.  Drawing the flame graph may have changed the selection, so the
    // section contents are rebuilt (the heights computed above are kept).
    let sections = bottom_sections(app);
    let constraints: Vec<Constraint> = needs.iter().map(|&n| Constraint::Length(n)).collect();
    let bottom_chunks = Layout::vertical(constraints).split(bottom_area);

        }
    }

//! Key event handling.

use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyModifiers};

use crate::app::{App, SortColumn, View};

pub fn handle_key_event(app: &mut App, key: KeyEvent) {
    // Any key press clears a transient info message.
    app.info = None;

    if app.input.is_some() {
        handle_search_input(app, key);
        return;
    }

    match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char('c') | KeyCode::Char('C') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
            app.quit();
            return;
        }
        KeyCode::Char('q') => {
            app.quit();
            return;
        }
        KeyCode::Tab => {
            app.toggle_view();
            return;
        }
        KeyCode::Char('r') => {
            app.reset();
            return;
        }
        KeyCode::Char('/') => {
            app.start_search();
            return;
        }
        _ => {}
    }

    match app.view {
        View::Flamegraph => handle_flamegraph_key(app, key),
        View::Top => handle_table_key(app, key),
    }
}

fn handle_search_input(app: &mut App, key: KeyEvent) {
    match key.code {
        KeyCode::Enter => app.submit_search_input(),
        KeyCode::Esc => app.cancel_search_input(),
        _ => {
            if let Some(input) = &mut app.input {
                input.handle_key(key);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn handle_flamegraph_key(app: &mut App, key: KeyEvent) {
    match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Down => app.select_child(),
        KeyCode::Char('k') | KeyCode::Up => app.select_parent(),
        KeyCode::Char('h') | KeyCode::Left => app.select_prev_sibling(),
        KeyCode::Char('l') | KeyCode::Right => app.select_next_sibling(),
        KeyCode::Char('f') => app.scroll_down(),
        KeyCode::Char('b') => app.scroll_up(),
        KeyCode::Char('G') => app.scroll_bottom(),
        KeyCode::Char('g') => app.scroll_top(),
        KeyCode::Enter => app.zoom_in(),
        KeyCode::Esc => app.zoom_out(),
        KeyCode::Char('#') => app.search_selected(),
        KeyCode::Char('n') => app.select_next_match(),
        KeyCode::Char('N') => app.select_prev_match(),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn handle_table_key(app: &mut App, key: KeyEvent) {
    match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Down => app.table_down(),
        KeyCode::Char('k') | KeyCode::Up => app.table_up(),
        KeyCode::Char('f') => {
            let page = app.table.page;
            app.table_page_down(page);
        }
        KeyCode::Char('b') => {
            let page = app.table.page;
            app.table_page_up(page);
        }
        KeyCode::Char('1') => app.set_sort_column(SortColumn::Total),
        KeyCode::Char('2') => app.set_sort_column(SortColumn::Own),
        KeyCode::Enter => app.table_select_function(),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let matches = cli().get_matches();
    let sorted = matches.get_flag("sorted");
    let echo = matches.get_flag("echo");
    let debug = matches.get_flag("debug");

    }

    let tick_rate = Duration::from_millis(250);
    let mut last_tick = Instant::now();
    while app.running {
        tui.terminal.draw(|frame| {
            let start = Instant::now();
            ui::render(app, frame);
            app.record_timing("render", start.elapsed());
        })?;

        // Wait for the next key press, resize or tick; each of them triggers
        // a redraw.
        loop {
            let timeout = tick_rate
                .checked_sub(last_tick.elapsed())
                .unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO);

    os.execv(bin_, [bin_, '/tmp/t/huge.txt'])
start=time.time()
got=0
first=None
while time.time()-start < 15:
    r,_,_ = select.select([fd],[],[],0.1)
    if r:
        try:
            data=os.read(fd, 65536)
        except OSError:
            break
        if data:
            if first is None: first=time.time()-start
            got+=len(data)
            if b'[hjkl' in data or got > 20000:
                break
print(f"{bin_}: first bytes after {first:.2f}s, total {time.time()-start:.2f}s, bytes {got}")
os.write(fd, b'q')
time.sleep(0.3)
try:
    os.kill(pid, 9)
except Exception: pass
EOF
